data.summary: F10 keeps stopping mainly because missing parts/AGV issues and nutrunner torque faults create repeated downtime, and andon missing-part events repeatedly stop the line.

findings.claim: F10's largest incident downtime comes from part shortages: supplier_short (high severity) has 22 incidents, 459.0 downtime_min, 366 cars lost, and agv_down (medium) has 58 incidents, 171.9 downtime_min, 138 cars lost.
Torque faults are the next major cause: controller_fault (medium) has 36 incidents and 451.7 downtime_min, and torque_out_of_range (medium) has 37 incidents and 186.5 downtime_min.
Andon data show missing_part causes the most stopped_line events, with 97 on shift A and 60 on shift B, while equipment has 66 stopped_line events on shift B.
Machine telemetry for F10's M-06 nutrunner shows repeated failure=1 rows, including overstrain_failure=1 with torque as high as 76.6 Nm, indicating machine-driven stops.
Floor context shows F10 is kitted with only a 9-minute line-side buffer and one worker per shift, with no lapsed certificates, so thin buffering rather than certification gaps exposes the line.

data.recommendation: Prioritize supplier-short and AGV-down parts for F10 kitting so the 9-minute line-side buffer does not deplete, and immediately inspect/repair the M-06 torque controller and worn socket, re-auditing joints since the last good torque.
